summary: Safe and in-rules if the gather either gets its own griddepcontrol.wait or is launched without the PDL attribute. The idea holds but its size is overstated: PDL can only hide w2's launch gap, prologue and first weight stage, not w13's last-wave tail work. Expect about 0.5-1.5% on bs=256 (3.4 us err on a 404.9 us row) and roughly +0.1-0.2% on the headline, so the scored number cannot confirm it. The readout is the prepare-time per-kernel event times with and without PDL, so no companion is needed.
justification: A. Plausible on H200: wg_kernel is persistent, runs one CTA per SM with a static item stride, and runs back to back in a graph, so PDL can overlap w2's launch latency, barrier init, chunk-table prologue, setmaxnreg and first weight bulk_g2s with w13's tail. The tail work itself cannot be overlapped. w2 cannot consume anything until griddepcontrol.wait returns, and that only happens once every w13 CTA has completed and flushed. Early w2 CTAs therefore sit on freed SMs and wait; they do not do useful GEMM work in the tail. The real saving is the inter-kernel gap plus w2's prologue and ring-fill latency, about 2-6 us at bs=256, with smaller savings at gather->w13. Weakest link: the hypothesis's numbers. It quotes w13 303 us + w2 148 us = 451 us, which is more than the 404.9 us shape total. The scored profiles of master's lineage show wg_kernel<true> 237.6-239.2 us and wg_kernel<false> 111.8-119.0 us (s5-bucket-gate job 4e4a0e26/7be125e9, align2 job c05a8f73). The '~19.5 us items, 10-20 us of idle SMs' figure then becomes a reason for a 2-4% target that PDL cannot reach. bs=256 err_ns is 3.3-3.4 us (about 0.8%), and the shape carries 1/6 of the score, so even a real 1% shape gain is about +0.17% on the headline against a CI of about +/-1.5%. The headline and the row can at most fail to refute it. The conjecture can only be confirmed or refuted by the prepare log ('PDL on' plus per-kernel event times with and without PDL on the same graph). The expected directions are consistent: bs=1/16/32/8 run Marlin, and bs=128 runs Marlin in both master profiles (B128 flag off), so they are flat controls. Separate correctness gap: item (1) PDL-launches wg_gather_kernel, but (3) gives the gather no griddepcontrol.wait. Its predecessor is the SGLang expert_map gather / moe_align_block_size, which is not ours and never triggers, so the trigger is implicit at its exit. PTX still only guarantees visibility of the primary's writes to a dependent after griddepcontrol.wait. Also, w13's pre-wait prologue reads block_experts/n_padded, and the claim that 'align completed before the w13 grid started' holds only if the gather waited. Require one of two things: give wg_gather_kernel a griddepcontrol.wait as its first statement, or (simpler, and nearly costless because align never triggers early) launch the gather with a plain <<<>>> launch and put PDL only on the w13 and w2 launches.
confounders: cuda-nvfp4-wgmma-rega-grouped-s5-copy-safe-bucket-gate (current BEST, the base of the wgmma path): bs=256 runs wgmma only when the prepare-time _wg_select timing selector sets wg_on_256, and the hypothesis re-runs that selector with PDL. If the flag flips in this run (off, or B128 on), the bs=256/bs=128 rows measure a path switch, not PDL. The log must print the final wg_on_128/wg_on_256 and the path each bucket took; a row move with a flipped flag is not attributable to PDL.

align-two-phase-port-from17 (on master, Marlin path only): no interaction while bs=256 is on wgmma, because _moe_wgmma still uses SGLang's moe_align_block_size at block 16. If the selector turns B256 off, bs=256 falls to Marlin with align2, which is a different and confounded comparison. Same remedy: log the chosen path.

align-parallel-per-expert-verify / triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack (align for T>32 on the Marlin path): these do not touch _moe_wgmma's align. They matter only through the same selector-flip route.

w2-marlin-atomic-add-small-m, post-expert-norm-triton-small-m, marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm, sglang-marlin-path-parity: their shapes or paths do not overlap this change (num_tokens <= 32, or Marlin at bs=128); no confounding beyond run-to-run noise on the control rows.
interference: No companion. The only area this change touches is three launches on the wgmma path at 128<=T<=512. The landed hypotheses that could interact do so only by flipping the bucket selector, and the run's log resolves that, not a revert run. The hypothesis already builds its own A/B into prepare: the same captured graph is timed with and without PDL, outputs are compared bit for bit, and per-kernel event times are printed. That in-process A/B has far less noise than a second scored run, which would cost a submit and still sit inside the 3.4 us err. A gain or a loss on the bs=256 row can be read through the prepare event times, so the result is interpretable without a companion. Ordering note from the hypothesis's own Risk section: wg-stream-k-tail-split targets the tail work PDL cannot reach, so the two are complementary, not duplicates.
rules_flags: Correctness: PDL-launching wg_gather_kernel without a griddepcontrol.wait leaves its reads of sorted_ids/block_experts/n_padded (and transitively w13's pre-wait prologue reads) without a formal visibility guarantee from the align kernel. Fix: plain launch for the gather (preferred), or griddepcontrol.wait as its first statement.

Standing policy (no per-call mutable state): state['wg_pdl'] must be decided once in prepare and only read in kernel_fn. No try/except-and-flip at call time, and no process-global toggle. cudaLaunchKernelEx's programmaticStreamSerialization attribute is per launch, not process-global, so it is allowed.

Scored-submit hazard: the hypothesis states 'The first measurement is an okc check, never a scored submit', but today's run is scored because checks are spent. Given that, the prepare-time bit-identity check (refilled graph replays, PDL vs non-PDL) and the three-state copy check must fall back to master's launches (wg_pdl=False) on any mismatch or launch error, never raise. A pre-wait read of wg_xs/wg_hs or of the w2 out buffer is the one bug class that would fail the judge's recheck.

Keep everything before griddepcontrol.wait limited to constant weights and the align outputs. That covers the err[1] launch marker write (per state, harmless) and the first weights-only bulk_g2s. The expect_tx byte count can include the B-slab bytes issued after the wait. No B-slab TMA, epilogue store or cache3 write may come before the wait.
No caching derived from inputs, no host sync, no work moved outside the timed call: PDL changes only the launch edge, which the graph captures. Precision path unchanged.
open_questions: Where do the 303/148 us per-kernel figures come from? The scored profiles show about 238/112-119 us. Re-derive the target from the profile; a realistic bs=256 expectation is 2-6 us (0.5-1.5%), not 10-20 us.

Is griddepcontrol.launch_dependents issued by one thread (the producer after its last stage) enough for the CTA on this toolchain? PTX treats the instruction per CTA, but confirm the consumer-side issue is either redundant or harmless.

With the 3.4 us err and a 1/6 shape weight, is a scored submit the right vehicle for a change whose expected headline effect is about +0.1-0.2%? It is safe and interpretable through the prepare log, but it will not register as a 'gain' under the CI rules even if it works.
